foundation: Barrot V3 remains the execution, security, preservation and verification foundation.

research.topic: Firelight compliance screening, FXRP staking liquidity and model-risk implications

event.reported_claim: Firelight said its compliance screening process had unstaked and returned 117,500 FXRP across 87 addresses and that it would roll back the blacklist process and unblock affected wallets.
event.primary_statement_status: No primary Firelight post or signed notice was located in this run.
event.source_independence: The reports appear to repeat the same underlying Firelight statement; they are not treated as four independent confirmations.
event.resolution_status: The announced rollback and current replacement-screening implementation were not independently verified.

official_mechanics.claim: Firelight launched on October 6, 2026 with its first cover for Sentora USD Protected Vault and Protected RWA Vaults; one shared Firelight Vault on Flare holds staked FXRP backing the covered portfolio.

stXRP represents FXRP deposited into Firelight; staked principal and compounded rewards are subject to slashing; fees fund emissions in FXRP; unstaking takes time to match 30-day cover periods; Firelight Cover is not insurance.
Flare Smart Accounts can mint FXRP from XRP and deposit it into Firelight in one flow; unstaking returns to FXRP before redemption to XRP.

quantitative_context.interpretation: Scale comparison only. Snapshot is not contemporaneous with the October 9 event and does not measure current Firelight stake or liquid float.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The screening event created a small, temporary FXRP unstaking and liquidity-distribution shock.
supporting_evidence: Secondary reports cite 117,500 FXRP returned across 87 addresses.
disconfirming_evidence: The reported amount is approximately 0.08161% of the later 143.98M FXRP supply snapshot.
Reports say funds were returned to original addresses; no XRP spot sale is evidenced.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Screening and wallet-access uncertainty could affect future Firelight participation more than immediate XRP market supply.
supporting_evidence: Firelight staking positions are subject to compliance screening, slashing and delayed unstaking.
disconfirming_evidence: No post-event deposit, withdrawal, stXRP discount or stake-retention series was verified.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The event had negligible direct XRP spot-price impact absent a demonstrated exchange sale or sustained net FXRP redemption.
supporting_evidence: Reported event size is below 0.1% of the later FXRP supply snapshot.
No exchange deposit, spot execution or net XRP sale is documented.
disconfirming_evidence: Wallet-level transaction reconciliation and subsequent flows remain unavailable.

unknowns: Primary Firelight statement and exact affected-address list.
Onchain transaction hashes for the 117,500 FXRP return.
Whether the announced rollback was completed and which screening policy replaced it.
Whether Hugo Philion's stated compensation was paid and to which eligible addresses.
Current Firelight stake, unstake queue, stXRP discount and cover-capacity utilization.
Whether affected funds were subsequently sold, restaked or redeployed.

prediction_engine.review_finding: The existing ledger claimed LATEST_OBSERVATION_AT_OR_BEFORE_HORIZON but only verified that a selected price/timestamp pair existed in the registered snapshot. It did not prove the selected observation was actually the latest observation at or before the cutoff/horizon. An earlier observation within the allowed lag could therefore be selected.
prediction_engine.correction: Require the issue price to be the unique latest observation at or before data_cutoff_utc and the outcome price to be the unique latest observation at or before target_end_at_utc. Reapply the same rule during metrics authorization so persisted timestamp edits fail closed.
regression_tests: Reject earlier issue observation when a later pre-cutoff observation exists.
Reject earlier outcome observation when a later pre-horizon observation exists.
Reject persisted outcome timestamp substitution even when price and lag fields are internally consistent.
Reject persisted issue timestamp substitution during metrics authorization.
